chapter_title: Cell: The Building Block of Life
subject: Biology (Science)
ground_truth_status: Human-verified via second-LLM audit (Gemini) against source PDF text and page footers
expected_concepts: Cell as the basic structural and functional unit of life
Limit of resolution of human eye (0.1 mm) and why microscopes are needed
Light microscope vs electron microscope, and Robert Hooke's discovery of the cell (1665)
Cell membrane / plasma membrane — selectively permeable, fluid-mosaic model (lipid bilayer + proteins)
Osmosis (movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane) vs diffusion (net movement of particles, higher to lower concentration)
Isotonic, hypotonic, hypertonic solutions and their effect on cells
Cell wall (plants, fungi, bacteria) — made of cellulose, provides rigidity, distinct from cell membrane
Prokaryotic cells (no true nucleus, nucleoid, no membrane-bound organelles) vs Eukaryotic cells (true nucleus, membrane-bound organelles)
Nucleus, nucleolus, chromatin, chromosomes, DNA and genes
Ribosomes (protein synthesis), Endoplasmic Reticulum (Rough ER vs Smooth ER), Golgi apparatus (packaging/shipping)
Lysosomes (cell's clean-up system / digestion of waste)
Mitochondria — 'powerhouse of the cell', outer/inner membrane, cristae, ATP production via cellular respiration
Plastids — chloroplasts (photosynthesis, chlorophyll), chromoplasts (pigments/colour), leucoplasts (colourless, food storage)
Vacuoles — storage and support, cell sap, plant cell turgidity/wilting
Cell division: Mitosis (2 genetically identical daughter cells) vs Meiosis (4 daughter cells, half chromosome number, occurs in reproductive organs)
Cell Theory: Schleiden (plants, 1838), Schwann (animals, 1839), Virchow (cells arise from pre-existing cells, 1855)
Contact inhibition and cancer/tumour formation from uncontrolled cell division
expected_objectives: Explain how the cell is the structural and functional unit of life
Describe how technological tools (microscopes) enabled discovery of cell structure
Identify and describe the functions of major cell organelles
Distinguish between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, and between plant and animal cells
Explain the processes of osmosis and diffusion using real-world examples
Describe how a cell grows, divides (mitosis and meiosis), and eventually dies
State the Cell Theory and its historical development

candidate_facts_for_tampering: Robert Hooke observed a cell in 1665 using a self-designed microscope (~200-300X magnification) — could change the year or the magnification power
Mitosis produces TWO genetically identical daughter cells; Meiosis produces FOUR daughter cells with HALF the chromosome number — could swap the two/four or omit 'half the chromosome number'
The limit of resolution of the human eye is 0.1 mm — could change the number
Cell Theory: Schleiden (plants, 1838), Schwann (animals, 1839), Virchow (pre-existing cells, 1855) — could swap which scientist did which contribution or the dates
Mitochondria have an outer membrane (smooth) and inner membrane (folded into cristae) — could invert which membrane is smooth vs folded
